newsitem.title: UK: All quiet on the Eurobond front - new issues traders.
newsitem.headline: All quiet on the Eurobond front - new issues traders.

text.p: The primary market came to a standstill on Monday, with little expected to ripple the pond until next year, new issues traders said.
"Its all gone quiet," a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank said. "Everyone started winding down a week ago and there is nothing very serious to be done before the end of the year."
"All syndicates have their eye firmly fixed on an early launch to hit the screens next year," he said.
Some syndicate sources said Argentina was expected to launch a jumbo mark bond before the end of the year with a likely 10-year maturity.
The issue could be for between 750 million and 1.0 billion marks at a five- or 10-year maturity, some dealers said.
"The amount is still open, it depends, they (Argentina) have not yet made up their mind but 1.0 billion marks is possible," a syndicate manager at a German bank said.
"It would be a benchmark," he added.
Another syndicate manager said Argentina was seeking longer-dated funds so a 10-year issue was most likely.
Its last 10-year issue -- launched in March and increased -- was priced to yield 475 basis points over Bunds via CSFB-Effectenbank and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The 10-year deal paid an 11.25 percent coupon and some said the issue could serve to help price the next bond. It was last trading at 410 b.p. over Bunds, dealers said.
CSFB and Deutsche were in the running to lead manage the transaction given their history of underwriting for sovereign borrowers this year, traders said.
Later, Slovak Bank Vseobecna Uverova Banka AS launched an expected 1.5 billion Slovak crown two-year bond which pays a 12.40 percent coupon.
The paper is listed in Bratislava and the deal was underwritten by Bankers Trust International.

"As VUB wants to attract more international investors, they launched a domestic bond in the Eurobond format to make it more appealing and understandable -- it has recognisable terms and conditions," a source close to the deal said.
The bond was priced to yield 50 b.p. over the average yield of the IFC 11.75 percent bonds due August 1999.
